facts.fact_text: According to the applicant, the demonstrations were conducted in a peaceful manner.
The applicant attended the demonstration of 12 January 2013.
The applicant attended the demonstration of 26 January 2013.
Shortly after the demonstration of 12 January 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse the assembly.
Shortly after the demonstration of 26 January 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse the assembly.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation of the demonstration of 12 January 2013.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation of the demonstration of 26 January 2013.
On the day of the applicant's arrest on 12 January 2013, an administrative-offence report (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) was issued in respect of the applicant.
On the day of the applicant's arrest on 26 January 2013, an administrative-offence report (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) was issued in respect of the applicant.
In the first case, the Nasimi District Court found that the applicant had participated in an unauthorised demonstration.
In the second case, the Nasimi District Court found that the applicant had participated in an unauthorised demonstration.

Before the amendments introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, which entered into force on 1 January 2013, any breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies was punishable under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 by a reprimand or a fine of AZN 7 to 13.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 entered into force on 1 January 2013.
Both of the applicant's arrests occurred after the amendments introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 were enacted.

At the time of the applicant's arrests, Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that participation in an assembly, a demonstration, a protest, a march or a picket which was not organised in accordance with the rules set forth under the legislation shall be punishable by a fine of AZN 300 to 600; or, depending on the circumstances of the case and the personality of the perpetrator of the offence, by community service for 160 to 200 hours or administrative detention for up to 15 days.

The administrative-offence report issued on 12 January 2013 stated that the applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (participation in a public assembly that had not been organised in accordance with the law).

The administrative-offence report issued on 26 January 2013 stated that the applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (participation in a public assembly that had not been organised in accordance with the law).
Shortly after the demonstration of 12 January 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse the assembly.
Shortly after the demonstration of 26 January 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse the assembly.

Report CommDH(2013)14 stated that the Commissioner is of the view that participants in peaceful assemblies should not be sanctioned for the mere fact of being present at and actively participating in the demonstration in question, provided they do not do anything illegal, violent or obscene in the course of it.

Report CommDH(2013)14 stated that the Commissioner urges the Azerbaijani authorities to ensure that no disproportionate sanction, which would undermine the fundamental right to peaceful assembly, is imposed.
According to the applicant, he was never served with a copy of the administrative-offence report relating to his arrest on 12 January 2013.
According to the applicant, he was never served with a copy of the administrative-offence report relating to his arrest on 26 January 2013.
According to the applicant, he was never served with other documents in his case file relating to his arrest on 12 January 2013.
According to the applicant, he was never served with other documents in his case file relating to his arrest on 26 January 2013.
According to the applicant, he was not given access to a lawyer after his arrest on 12 January 2013 or while in police custody following that arrest.
According to the applicant, he was not given access to a lawyer after his arrest on 26 January 2013 or while in police custody following that arrest.
According to the applicant, members of the public were not allowed to attend the hearing in the first case before the Nasimi District Court.
According to the applicant, members of the public were not allowed to attend the hearing in the second case before the Nasimi District Court.
According to the applicant, in the first case he was not given an opportunity to hire a lawyer of his own choice.
According to the applicant, in the second case he was not given an opportunity to hire a lawyer of his own choice.
At the court hearing in the second case before the Nasimi District Court, a State-funded lawyer was appointed to assist the applicant.
The record of the court hearing in the second case before the Nasimi District Court shows that the State-funded lawyer made oral submissions.
In his oral submissions at the second case hearing, the State-funded lawyer briefly stated that there had been elements of the administrative offence in the applicant's actions.
In his oral submissions at the second case hearing, the State-funded lawyer asked the Nasimi District Court to adopt a fair decision.
In his appeals before the Baku Court of Appeal, the applicant complained that the hearings before the respective first-instance courts had not been fair.
In the first case, the applicant was not represented before the Baku Court of Appeal by a lawyer.

At the appellate court hearing in the second case before the Baku Court of Appeal, the applicant was represented by the same State-funded lawyer who had represented him before the Nasimi District Court.
